_doc: The free asset library (tools/assets/README.md). Every entry: loop (which visual loop owns placing it), use (where it goes in the game), real (the real Midwestern thing it matches, the real-world rule). src defaults to polyhaven (CC0). fetch.py refuses any licence but CC0-1.0 and CC-BY-4.0.

fire_hydrant.use: street fire hydrants in the grass strip, one a block (hydrants #961)
fire_hydrant.real: red dry-barrel US hydrant, two hose nozzles + pumper nozzle, ~0.8 m tall (AWWA C502)

water_manhole_cover.use: manhole lids in the street over sewer and water lines
water_manhole_cover.real: cast-iron 0.6-0.7 m round lid, as on every Indiana street

concrete_road_barrier.use: work zones, road closures, bridge approaches
concrete_road_barrier.real: Jersey barrier (New Jersey-shape concrete median barrier, 0.8 m tall)
concrete_road_barrier.check: reads as a block barrier with lifting loops, not a true New Jersey profile: fine for work zones

concrete_road_barrier_02.use: work zones and dead ends, second shape

metal_trash_can.use: curbside cans and alley cans by garages
metal_trash_can.real: galvanised steel cans, still common in Midwestern alleys

trashbag.use: trash bags out at the curb on pickup day

street_lamp_01.real: ornamental cast-iron acorn/lantern lamp like the courthouse-square lamps in Marion, Fairmount and many Indiana downtowns
street_lamp_01.check: 4 m tall: confirm it reads as a post-top lantern, not a European wall lamp

modular_electricity_poles.use: wooden utility poles with crossarms and pole transformers along streets and county roads
modular_electricity_poles.real: Class 4-5 wooden distribution poles with pole-top transformers (Duke Energy/Indiana Michigan Power style)
modular_electricity_poles.parts: three ready poles: ['preset_01_*'], ['preset_02_*'], ['preset_03_*'] (01/03 carry transformers); loose parts for building your own

garden_hose_wall_mounted_01.real: wall hose reel by the spigot

garden_sprinkler_01.use: lawn sprinklers in summer front yards

plastic_monobloc_chair_01.real: white resin monobloc chair, on half the porches in Grant County

wooden_picnic_table.use: park shelters, school yards, backyards, church lawns
wooden_picnic_table.real: classic wooden picnic table with attached benches (park department style)

covered_car.use: car under a tarp in driveways and farmyards (stored cars)
covered_car.real: car cover on a stored car

wooden_ladder.use: ladders on construction sites and against garages

modular_street_seating.use: benches on downtown sidewalks and plazas
modular_street_seating.real: slatted metal and wood street bench
modular_street_seating.check: contemporary style: fine for rebuilt streetscapes, not 1900s squares

planter_box_02.use: sidewalk planters in front of shops

standing_chalkboard_01.use: A-frame sidewalk signs outside diners, bars and shops

outdoor_table_chair_set_01.use: sidewalk tables outside cafes and diners

security_light.use: wall-pack security lights on shops, factories, barns

flood_lights.use: ball field and lot flood light heads
flood_lights.parts: kit: '*standing_single_*' one light on a stand, '*wall_*' wall light, '*double*' twin heads

utility_box_02.use: electric cabinets by substations and signals

modular_chainlink_fence.use: chain-link around ball fields, schools, industry, substations
modular_chainlink_fence.real: galvanised chain-link fence, 6 ft (1.8 m), top rail and line posts

rollershutter_door.use: overhead coiling doors on loading docks, garages, fire stations
rollershutter_door.parts: clean: ['rollershutter_door']; graffiti: ['rollershutter_door_graffiti'] (rare in small Indiana towns)

rollershutter_window_01.use: security shutters on closed or older shop fronts
rollershutter_window_01.parts: clean and graffiti versions, like rollershutter_door

modular_fire_escape.use: fire escapes on the backs of 2-4 storey downtown blocks
modular_fire_escape.real: steel fire escape stairs on 1890s-1920s Indiana commercial blocks
modular_fire_escape.parts: kit: platform, stairs, railings, ladder pieces stacked per storey

modular_metal_gutter.use: gutters and downspouts on commercial and industrial buildings

plastic_crate_03.use: stacked crates at docks, groceries, farmers' market

cardboard_box_01.use: boxes at docks and moving days

modular_industrial_pipes_01.use: pipe racks on factories, gas regulator stations

overhead_crane.use: outdoor gantry crane at steel and precast yards
overhead_crane.real: overhead bridge/gantry crane (steel fabricators, precast plants)

barrel_03.use: 55-gallon drums at farm shops, factories, burn barrels
barrel_03.real: 55 US gal steel drum (0.9 m tall)

metal_jerrycan.use: fuel cans in farm shops and garages

old_tyre.use: old tires by farm shops and junk piles, silage-tarp tires
old_tyre.real: car tire; farmers weight silage tarps with old tires

tree_stump_01.use: stumps in woods, fencerows and cleared lots

dead_tree_trunk.use: fallen logs on woods floors and creek banks
dead_tree_trunk.real: downed log in an Indiana woodlot

dry_branches_medium_01.use: brush and fallen branches in woods and fencerows

boulder_01.use: glacial erratic boulders at field corners, lanes and yards
boulder_01.real: glacial erratic (Grant County is glacial till; farmers pile field stones at corners)

rock_moss_set_01.use: fieldstone piles along fencerows and creek riprap

veh_sedan_fusion_2016.author: Gizmitt
veh_sedan_fusion_2016.name: 2016 Ford Fusion Photoscan (cleaned and resized for the game)
veh_sedan_fusion_2016.real: 2016 Ford Fusion sedan, 4.87 m long (Ford spec)

weathered_plank_siding.real: unpainted weathered barn siding on 1900s bank and English barns

wood_peeling_paint_weathered.use: red/white barns with peeling paint (tint the albedo)

white_planks_clean.use: painted wood clapboard and porch ceilings close up
white_planks_clean.real: painted wood lap siding on pre-war houses

red_brick.real: red common brick, running bond, 1880s-1920s Indiana Main Street blocks

red_brick_03.use: sooty older brick: factories, rear walls

factory_brick.real: red-brown factory face brick (Marion's glass/paper mills)

painted_brick.use: painted side walls of downtown blocks (tint the albedo, ghost signs)

yellow_brick.real: buff/yellow brick common on Indiana postwar ranches

concrete_block_wall.use: CMU walls: garages, shops, small factories, dugouts

rough_block_wall.use: split-face block on newer shops and churches

rusty_corrugated_iron.use: old machine sheds, corn crib roofs, grain bin roofs
rusty_corrugated_iron.real: galvanised corrugated steel gone to rust

box_profile_metal_sheet.use: pole barns and newer farm shops, metal roofs on houses
box_profile_metal_sheet.real: ribbed steel panel (R-panel) on post-frame buildings

factory_wall.real: insulated steel wall panel on pre-engineered metal buildings

bitumen.use: flat roofs of downtown blocks, schools and shops

worn_asphalt.use: old city streets and parking lots
worn_asphalt.real: aged asphalt with raveling and leaf litter

tarred_gravel.real: chip seal (tar and chip), the surface of most Grant County roads

concrete_pavement.check: described as pavers; compare to a 5-ft scored sidewalk slab

playground_sand.use: sand volleyball, sandboxes, ball diamond infields (tint)

withered_grass.use: dormant November-March grass, CRP and ditch grass

sparse_grass.use: worn lawns, foul lines, lane edges

dry_decay_leaves.use: October-November leaf litter under trees (seasons loop)

muddy_tracks.use: field entrances and farm lanes in spring

white_sandstone_blocks_02.use: ashlar stone on courthouses, banks, churches, post offices
white_sandstone_blocks_02.real: stand-in for Indiana (Bedford) oolitic limestone ashlar
white_sandstone_blocks_02.check: compare to Grant County Courthouse limestone; tint toward grey-buff

beige_wall_001.use: EIFS fronts and tenant towers of 1990s-2010s strip centres (tinted to the wall colour)
beige_wall_001.real: exterior insulation and finish system: fine sand-finish acrylic stucco over foam, the dress of every 1990s-2010s Indiana strip centre and pad restaurant

large_sandstone_blocks.use: dressed stone bases, belt courses and cornices of downtown blocks, banks and office buildings (its shading only, tinted to the stone colour)
large_sandstone_blocks.real: sawn Indiana (Bedford) limestone ashlar, the base and trim of nearly every Indiana courthouse-square bank and office block

kloofendal_48d_partly_cloudy_puresky.use: summer fair-weather cumulus sky for reflections and ambient

_rejected.exterior_aircon_unit: wall-mounted split units (Europe/Asia); US houses have a square condenser on a pad: still code-built
_rejected.propane_tank: red European gas bottle; US 20 lb cylinders are white/grey
_rejected.utility_box_01: blue European street cabinet with high-voltage stickers
_rejected.roof_07/roof_09/roof_3/roof_tiles: clay tile roofs: almost none in Grant County. Poly Haven has no asphalt shingle photo yet (keep code-built shingles)
_rejected.pine_tree_01/fir_tree_01/island_tree_*: scanned trees are 2-17 million triangles: far too heavy for a town full of trees
